slot.brief: Give four orders (ionisation enthalpy, electronegativity, electron gain enthalpy, atomic radius across a set of elements); find the incorrectly stated trend.

stem: For the elements $\text{Na}$, $\text{Mg}$, $\text{Al}$ and $\text{Si}$, which stated order is incorrect?

verdicts.working: Across period 3, the magnitudes are approximately Si: 134, Na: 53, Al: 44 kJ mol⁻¹; thus Na has a greater magnitude than Al, contrary to (D).

working:
Electron-gain enthalpy magnitudes: $\text{Si} > \text{Na} > \text{Al} > \text{Mg}$. The stated order swaps $\text{Na}$ and $\text{Al}$.

Independent check: Across period 3, the magnitudes are approximately Si: 134, Na: 53, Al: 44 kJ mol⁻¹; thus Na has a greater magnitude than Al, contrary to (D).
solution:
Across period 3, the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is approximately Si: $134$, Na: $53$, Al: $44$, and Mg: $0$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Thus, the correct order is $\text{Si} > \text{Na} > \text{Al} > \text{Mg}$; the stated order incorrectly places Al above Na.
